subject.title: feat(durable): add opt-in workflow worker loop

question: Should the durable workflow worker become a core runtime surface now, and if so which runtime owner should start and stop the env-gated worker after PR1-PR4 settle?
rationale: The PR adds a new background execution surface and env controls for durable workflow work; choosing the lifecycle owner and accepting that core product direction is maintainer policy, not a mechanical repair choice.

options.title: Pause, then wire and prove
options.body: Wait for the upstream durable stack to settle, wire the worker into the chosen lifecycle owner, and require live default-disabled plus opt-in execution proof before merge.

options.title: Accept library-only worker surface
options.body: Allow this PR to remain an internal callable worker library, but narrow the PR body/docs so it does not claim product-level worker enablement yet.

options.title: Defer the worker loop
options.body: Keep PR1-PR4 focused on durable state/recovery and move production worker execution to a later maintainer-sponsored design slice.

recommendation.title: Pause, then wire and prove
recommendation.body: Wait for the upstream durable stack to settle, wire the worker into the chosen lifecycle owner, and require live default-disabled plus opt-in execution proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing owner for the core durable runtime product decision and adjacent state/command surfaces.
